question: Under Section 1-10 of the Illinois Real Estate License Act, the term "employee" (or a derivative of it) may be construed to include an independent contractor relationship between a sponsoring broker and a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent only if what condition is met?
choice_a: A written agreement exists that clearly establishes and states the relationship
choice_b: The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation approves the arrangement in advance
choice_c: The parties have worked together for at least one year
choice_d: The independent contractor carries separate errors and omissions insurance
explanation: Sec. 1-10 states that "employee" shall be construed to include an independent contractor relationship, "provided that a written agreement exists that clearly establishes and states the relationship."

question: Section 1-10's definition of "employee" addresses the relationship between a sponsoring broker and which other license types?
choice_a: A managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent
choice_b: A title insurance agent or escrow officer
choice_c: An appraiser or home inspector
choice_d: A mortgage loan originator
explanation: Sec. 1-10 refers to the relationship "between a sponsoring broker and a managing broker, broker, or a residential leasing agent."

question: Under Section 10-15(a), no compensation may be paid to an unlicensed person in exchange for the person doing what?
choice_a: Performing licensed activities in violation of the Act
choice_b: Referring a friend to a licensee for a home purchase
choice_c: Staging a property for sale
choice_d: Posting a for-sale-by-owner advertisement
explanation: Sec. 10-15(a): "No compensation may be paid to any unlicensed person in exchange for the person performing licensed activities in violation of this Act."

question: Per Section 10-15(b), a court action to recover compensation for a service that this Act restricts to licensees may be maintained only if what is true?
choice_a: The person was duly licensed as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent under the Act at the time the act or service was performed
choice_b: The person filed a written complaint with the Department within 30 days
choice_c: The compensation sought is less than $5,000
choice_d: The service was performed under written contract regardless of licensure
explanation: Sec. 10-15(b) bars suits for such compensation "unless the person was duly licensed hereunder as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent under this Act at the time that any such act was done or service performed."

question: Under Section 10-15(c), a licensee may offer compensation, prizes, merchandise, services, rebates, or discounts to an unlicensed person under which circumstance?
choice_a: When that person is a party to a contract to buy or sell real estate, or a party to a contract for the lease of real estate, and the offer complies with subdivision (35) of subsection (a) of Section 20-20
choice_b: When that person has completed a pre-licensing course
choice_c: When that person is a licensed appraiser assisting with the transaction
choice_d: When the offer is approved by RESPA regulations
explanation: Sec. 10-15(c) permits such offers to "an unlicensed person who is a party to a contract to buy or sell real estate or is a party to a contract for the lease of real estate, so long as the offer complies with the provisions of subdivision (35) of subsection (a) of Section 20-20."

question: Section 10-15(d) allows a licensee to offer cash, gifts, prizes, awards, coupons, merchandise, rebates, or chances to win a game of chance to a consumer as an inducement to use the licensee's services under what condition?
choice_a: Even if the licensee and consumer do not ultimately enter into a broker-client relationship, so long as the offer is not prohibited by any other law and complies with subdivision (35) of subsection (a) of Section 20-20
choice_b: Only after a signed brokerage agreement is executed
choice_c: Only if the consumer is a first-time home buyer
choice_d: Only if the value of the inducement does not exceed $100
explanation: Sec. 10-15(d) permits such inducements "even if the licensee and consumer do not ultimately enter into a broker-client relationship so long as the offer complies with the provisions of subdivision (35) of subsection (a) of Section 20-20," and if not prohibited by other law.

question: Under Section 10-15(e), a licensee is prohibited from paying compensation to an unlicensed person in exchange for a referral of real estate services when that unlicensed person is in what position?
choice_a: Not or will not become a party to a real estate transaction
choice_b: A relative of the licensee
choice_c: A former client of the licensee's brokerage
choice_d: A resident of another state
explanation: Sec. 10-15(e): "A licensee shall not pay compensation to an unlicensed person who is not or will not become a party to a real estate transaction in exchange for a referral of real estate services."

question: Section 10-15(f) states that nothing in Section 10-15 shall be construed as waiving or abrogating the provisions of which federal law?
choice_a: The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA), 88 Stat. 1724
choice_b: The Truth in Lending Act
choice_c: The Fair Housing Act
choice_d: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act
explanation: Sec. 10-15(f): "Nothing in this Section shall be construed as waiving or abrogating the provisions of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA), 88 Stat. 1724."

question: Section 10-15 of the Illinois Real Estate License Act is scheduled to be repealed on what date?
choice_a: January 1, 2030
choice_b: January 1, 2025
choice_c: August 9, 2019
choice_d: December 31, 2029
explanation: The excerpt notes: "(Section scheduled to be repealed on January 1, 2030)" directly under the 225 ILCS 454/10-15 citation.

question: Per Section 10-20(a), a licensee may perform activities as a licensee only for whom?
choice_a: The licensee's sponsoring broker
choice_b: Any broker who requests the licensee's assistance
choice_c: A managing broker approved by the Department
choice_d: The client directly, bypassing the brokerage
explanation: Sec. 10-20(a): "A licensee may perform activities as a licensee only for the licensee's sponsoring broker."

question: Under Section 10-20(b), every broker who employs licensees or has an independent contractor relationship with a licensee must have what with each such licensee?
choice_a: A written employment or independent contractor agreement
choice_b: A surety bond filed with the Department
choice_c: A quarterly performance review
choice_d: A notarized fee-splitting disclosure
explanation: Sec. 10-20(b): "Every broker who employs licensees or has an independent contractor relationship with a licensee shall have a written employment or independent contractor agreement with each such licensee."

question: Per Section 10-20(b), the broker who holds the written employment or independent contractor agreement with a licensee must occupy what role for that licensee?
choice_a: That licensee's sponsoring broker
choice_b: A co-managing broker of equal standing
choice_c: A referral partner only
choice_d: A designated agent for disclosure purposes only
explanation: Sec. 10-20(b) states: "The broker having this written employment or independent contractor agreement with the licensee must be that licensee's sponsoring broker."

question: Under Section 10-20(c), the written employment or independent contractor agreement between a sponsoring broker and licensee shall address the relationship terms including, without limitation, which of the following?
choice_a: Supervision, duties, compensation, and termination process
choice_b: Marketing budget, office hours, and vacation policy
choice_c: Errors and omissions insurance premiums
choice_d: Multiple listing service dues
explanation: Sec. 10-20(c): the agreement "shall address the employment or independent contractor relationship terms, including without limitation supervision, duties, compensation, and termination process."

question: Under Section 10-20(d-5), if a written agreement provides for an independent contractor relationship that clearly states and establishes that relationship, what governs the licensee's conduct of brokerage activities?
choice_a: The specific provisions of this Act
choice_b: The Internal Revenue Service's independent contractor test
choice_c: The National Association of Realtors' Code of Ethics
choice_d: General common-law agency principles only
explanation: Sec. 10-20(d-5): "If a written agreement provides for an independent contractor relationship that clearly states and establishes that relationship, the specific provisions of this Act shall control for licensee's conduct of brokerage activities."

question: Under Section 10-20(e), notwithstanding an existing employment or independent contractor agreement, a sponsoring broker may pay compensation directly to what kind of entity?
choice_a: A business entity solely owned by the licensee that was formed for the purpose of receiving compensation earned by the licensee
choice_b: Any LLC nominated in writing by the licensee's spouse
choice_c: A licensed corporate brokerage unrelated to the licensee
choice_d: A trust administered by the Department
explanation: Sec. 10-20(e) allows payment "to a business entity solely owned by that licensee that has been formed for the purpose of receiving compensation earned by the licensee."

question: Per Section 10-20(e), does a business entity that receives a licensee's compensation under that subsection need to be licensed under the Act?
choice_a: No, such a business entity shall not be required to be licensed under the Act
choice_b: Yes, it must hold a corporate broker license
choice_c: Yes, but only if it has more than one employee
choice_d: No, but it must register annually with the Department for a fee
explanation: Sec. 10-20(e): "A business entity that receives compensation from a sponsoring broker as provided for in this subsection (e) shall not be required to be licensed under this Act."

question: Under Section 10-20(e), a business entity receiving a licensee's compensation may be owned by the licensee together with the licensee's spouse only under what condition?
choice_a: The spouse and licensee are both licensed and sponsored by the same sponsoring broker, or the spouse is not also licensed
choice_b: The spouse holds a separate managing broker license in another state
choice_c: The spouse is named as a co-signer on the brokerage's errors and omissions policy
choice_d: The couple has been married for at least five years
explanation: Sec. 10-20(e) requires the entity to be owned solely by the licensee, "or by the licensee together with the licensee's spouse, but only if the spouse and licensee are both licensed and sponsored by the same sponsoring broker or the spouse is not also licensed."

question: The current version of Section 10-20 cites a Public Act with an effective date of what?
explanation: The excerpt's source line for Sec. 10-20 reads: "(Source: P.A. 103-1039, eff. 1-1-25.)"

question: Under Section 10-25, a written brokerage agreement must, at minimum, provide for what regarding its duration?
choice_a: Automatic expiration within a definite period of time
choice_b: A renewable five-year term
choice_c: Automatic renewal unless the licensee objects
choice_d: A minimum term of 90 days
explanation: Sec. 10-25 requires every written brokerage agreement to "provide for automatic expiration within a definite period of time."

question: Under Section 10-25, if a written brokerage agreement's term is longer than one year, what right must it give the client, and with what maximum notice period?
choice_a: A right to terminate the agreement annually by giving no more than 30 days' prior written notice
choice_b: A right to terminate at any time with 10 days' oral notice
choice_c: A right to renegotiate commission every six months
choice_d: A right to terminate only with the sponsoring broker's written consent
explanation: Sec. 10-25: if the term is longer than one year, the agreement must "provide the client with a right to terminate the agreement annually by giving no more than 30 days' prior written notice."

question: Under Section 10-25, what is the legal effect of a written brokerage agreement that fails to include the required expiration/termination provision?
choice_a: The agreement shall be void
choice_b: The agreement is automatically capped at 30 days
choice_c: The agreement is voidable only at the client's election
choice_d: The Department may impose a fine but the agreement remains valid
explanation: Sec. 10-25: "Any written brokerage agreement not containing such a provision shall be void."

question: Per Section 10-25, when the license of a sponsoring broker is suspended or revoked, what happens to a brokerage agreement associated with that sponsoring broker?
choice_a: It is deemed to expire upon the effective date of the suspension or revocation
choice_b: It transfers automatically to the Department for administration
choice_c: It remains in effect until its stated expiration date regardless of the suspension
choice_d: It converts to a month-to-month agreement
explanation: Sec. 10-25: "When the license of any sponsoring broker is suspended or revoked, any brokerage agreement with the sponsoring broker shall be deemed to expire upon the effective date of the suspension or revocation."

question: The version of Section 10-25 quoted in the Act cites a Public Act effective on what date?
explanation: The excerpt's source line for Sec. 10-25 reads: "(Source: P.A. 103-236, eff. 1-1-24.)"

question: Under Section 15-15(b), does a licensee representing a client breach a duty to that client merely by showing alternative properties to prospective buyers or tenants?
choice_a: No -- showing alternative properties does not by itself breach a duty or obligation to the client
choice_b: Yes -- it constitutes an automatic breach of fiduciary duty
choice_c: Only if the alternative property is listed by a competing brokerage
choice_d: Only if the client has not signed an exclusive brokerage agreement
explanation: Sec. 15-15(b): "A licensee representing a client does not breach a duty or obligation to the client by showing alternative properties to prospective buyers or tenants."

question: Per Section 15-15(b), a licensee does not breach a duty to a client by showing properties in which that client is interested to whom?
choice_a: Other prospective buyers or tenants
choice_b: The client's family members only
choice_c: Licensees at a different brokerage
choice_d: The seller's attorney
explanation: Sec. 15-15(b) covers "showing properties in which the client is interested to other prospective buyers or tenants" as not, by itself, a breach of duty.

question: Under Section 15-15(b), merely making or preparing contemporaneous offers or contracts to purchase or lease the same property for multiple clients does what to the licensee's duty to those clients?
choice_a: Does not, by itself, breach the licensee's duty or obligation to the clients
choice_b: Automatically terminates the brokerage agreement with both clients
choice_c: Requires the licensee to withdraw representation from both clients
choice_d: Requires Department pre-approval before proceeding
explanation: Sec. 15-15(b) lists "making or preparing contemporaneous offers or contracts to purchase or lease the same property" among the actions that do not breach a duty to the client.

question: Under Section 15-15(b), what must a licensee provide to all clients for whom the licensee is preparing or making contemporaneous offers or contracts to purchase or lease the same property?
choice_a: Written disclosure
choice_b: A verbal warning at the time of showing
choice_c: A reduced commission rate
choice_d: A copy of the competing client's offer amount
explanation: Sec. 15-15(b): "a licensee shall provide written disclosure to all clients for whom the licensee is preparing or making contemporaneous offers or contracts to purchase or lease the same property."

question: Under Section 15-15(b), if a client involved in a contemporaneous-offer situation requests a referral, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Refer that client to another designated agent
choice_b: Decline the request and continue representing both clients
choice_c: Terminate the brokerage agreement with all clients involved
choice_d: Report the request to the Department within 5 business days
explanation: Sec. 15-15(b) requires the licensee to "refer to another designated agent any client that requests such referral."

question: Per Section 5-70(f), the subject areas of continuing education courses recommended by the Board and approved by the Department are meant to protect the professionalism of the industry, the consumer, and the public, and to do what else?
choice_a: Prevent violations of the Act
choice_b: Increase Department licensing revenue
choice_c: Reduce the number of licensed brokers statewide
choice_d: Standardize commission rates across the industry
explanation: Sec. 5-70(f): the CE subject areas "shall be meant to protect the professionalism of the industry, the consumer, and the public and prevent violations of this Act."

question: Which of the following is explicitly listed among the continuing education subject areas in Section 5-70(f)?
choice_a: Antitrust
choice_b: Loan underwriting standards
choice_c: Title insurance procedures
choice_d: Municipal zoning ordinances
explanation: Sec. 5-70(f)(2) lists "antitrust" as one of the recommended continuing education subject areas.

question: Section 5-70(f) lists both "property management" and a separate, more specialized item covering a specific property type. What is that separate item?
choice_a: Farm property management
choice_b: Multi-family property management
choice_c: Commercial property management
choice_d: Vacation rental property management
explanation: Sec. 5-70(f) lists "(6) property management" and, separately, "(8) farm property management" as distinct continuing education subject areas.
